previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a homeless man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol and polysubstance use, was admitted after being found in an alley with chest pain following a reported assault where he was punched near his implantable defibrillator and had his medications stolen. He had consumed a large amount of vodka that morning and experienced hypoglycemia, which resolved with treatment. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction, with negative troponins and a normal EKG, and imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary issues. He was managed for alcohol withdrawal using CIWA-guided diazepam and symptom control. Despite medical recommendations, he became impatient with care, declined further observation, and left against medical advice. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was advised to resume his home medications and follow up with cardiology and primary care.

are low.  There is no focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. 
A left chest wall pacemaker with a single lead in the right ventricle is
present.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette appears slightly enlarged.  The bones
are intact.  The imaged upper abdomen is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ man with altered mental status.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging was obtained through the brain without the
administration of intravenous contrast material.  Coronal and sagittal
reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or territorial
infarction.  Ventricles and sulci are normal in size and configuration.  There
is mild mucosal thickening of the left maxillary sinus.  The remainder of the
visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells and middle ear cavities are
clear.  There is no acute fracture.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

INDICATION:  ___ man with altered mental status.  Question fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging was obtained through the cervical spine without
the administration of intravenous contrast material.  Coronal and sagittal
reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute fracture or traumatic malalignment or
prevertebral soft tissue swelling.  The vertebral body heights are maintained.
There are mild degenerative changes most prominent at C6-C7 where there is
disc space narrowing and both anterior and posterior osteophytes, which may
predispose to cord injury.  The visualized lung apices are clear.  The soft
tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute fracture or traumatic malalignment.
2.  Mild degenerative changes with small posterior osteophytes as described
above which may predispose to cord injury.
